definition: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is a language model benchmark consisting of 2,500 questions across a broad range of subjects.
details: It was created jointly by the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI and publicly released in January 2025.

explainer.lead: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is a 2,500-question test for language models, covering a broad range of subjects. It gives researchers a common way to compare how accurately different models answer demanding questions.

tiers.eli5: HLE is like one giant school quiz with 2,500 questions from many subjects. Different language models take the same quiz, and their scores show how many answers they get right.
tiers.practitioner: Use HLE to compare language models on the same fixed set of 2,500 questions and report the proportion answered correctly. Break results down by subject where possible, because a single overall score can conceal uneven performance.
tiers.paperLevel: Let Q be HLE's set of 2,500 questions; for model outputs a_q and reference answers r_q, accuracy = (1/2500) * sum over q in Q of I(a_q = r_q). HLE was created jointly by the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI and publicly released in January 2025.

explainer.example: If a model answers 2,000 of the 2,500 questions correctly, its accuracy is 2,000 / 2,500 = 0.80, or 80%.

usedIn.name: Language model evaluation
usedIn.detail: Provides a shared question set for comparing answer accuracy across models.

usedIn.name: Cross-subject question answering
usedIn.detail: Tests performance across a broad range of subjects rather than one narrow domain.

explainer.measures: HLE measures how accurately a language model answers its 2,500 questions across a broad range of subjects.
howScored: Give each model the same set of questions.
Compare its answers with the correct answers.
Report the proportion of questions answered correctly.
caveats: One overall accuracy score can hide large differences between subjects.
Scores describe performance on this fixed question set, not every aspect of real-world usefulness.
